What's next

From proof of concept to a proven field tool

The methods work on simulations and hold up under honest testing. To prove them on real wells, we need a few specific kinds of data. Each item below is backed by what our tests showed it would unlock.

The data that would make the difference

1

A long real history

At least one full year of the company's real records, ideally two or more, so it spans several monsoons.

Unlocks: proof on real wells of the 12-week accuracy we saw on the digital twin, and the first test of forecasting through a monsoon.

2

Where each well is

Coordinates, or a coarse grid if exact locations are sensitive.

Unlocks: the well-to-well network model on real wells, plus local rainfall. Without locations, our tests showed finding neighbours is no better than chance.

3

Continuous water-level logging

A reading every few minutes, including while the pump is off, not only when a pump starts and stops.

Unlocks: link strengths within about 10% instead of about 30% too high. In tests, it also sharply improved spotting wells exposed to their neighbours.

4

Sensor calibration records

When each sensor was installed, checked, reset or replaced.

Unlocks: catching drifting sensors. In our tests, a sensor drifting 4–5 m fooled every model, because it looks exactly like a falling water table.

5

A geology map of cracks

Mapped lineaments (fracture zones) for the well fields, and drilling logs showing where water was struck.

Unlocks: knowing who is connected. Without it, the network model underestimated interference by about a third.

6

One short pumping test

Stop one busy well for 12 hours and log the wells around it minute by minute.

Unlocks: the exact link and delay between specific wells, which daily data cannot reveal, and a real-world check before any pumping advice is given.

The road ahead

Now

Real long-term data

Run the full test suite on real records: forecasts, ranges, rainfall and pumping effects. Report real accuracy side by side with the simulations.

Next

Early warning of dry wells

A 7-day warning for wells at risk of running dry, so operators can act before a pump runs empty. This is in development.

Then

Area-wide planning

With locations and a pumping test: map pressure-point wells, show how easing pumping in one place helps the neighbours, and assess new borewells before they are drilled.

What we will not claim until then

Real-world accuracy of months-ahead forecasts, the true strength of well-to-well links in Bengaluru, or anything beyond 12 weeks ahead. The simulations show the methods can work. Real records will show how well.

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
